identity.title: Make runtime governance decisions executable rather than observational

human_pressure.one_screen_brief: Move Ailuros one step from post-run explanation toward real runtime governance. Using the existing runtime/policy-gate/wrapped-tool path, prove every consequential tool/action request receives an explicit governance decision before execution. ALLOW executes once, BLOCK executes zero times, and review/authority-required executes zero times until separately resolved. Record truthful timeline evidence for every branch. Do not build orchestration infrastructure.
human_pressure.why_now: Ailuros already records runs, policy decisions, evidence, replay and audit. The product boundary now needs an executable pre-action gate rather than another diagnostic surface.
do_not_misread: Reuse existing decision names/states when equivalent semantics already exist.
This pack does not add an authority workflow UI or scheduler.
red_lines: No dashboard, server write API, MCP Gateway, scheduler, agent orchestrator, adapter marketplace, workflow engine or new database.
Replay stays read-only and audit must not recompute policy.

machine_core.goal: Establish one canonical pre-execution governance path where execution is impossible until the existing policy/runtime boundary has produced an explicit decision.
invariants: BLOCK invokes the tool zero times.
Review/authority-required invokes the tool zero times before separate authorization/review resolution.
ALLOW invokes the tool exactly once.
Execution never precedes its governance decision.
Timeline evidence represents decision and execution/non-execution truthfully.
Replay remains read-only and audit remains evidence-reading rather than policy recomputation.

observable_effect.assertion: Execution occurs exactly once only for an explicit allow-equivalent decision; deny/block and pending-review/authority decisions cause zero tool calls and produce auditable evidence.

failure_semantics: Unknown is never treated as allow.
A policy block is not a tool execution failure.
An allowed tool failure remains distinct from policy denial.

steps.title: Characterize current enforcement semantics
details: Locate the existing canonical wrapped-tool / before-tool-call / policy-gate path and existing decision vocabulary.
Write deterministic regressions for allow, block and any existing review/authority-required equivalent before changing production code.

steps.title: Close only the missing pre-execution gate
details: Ensure the tool cannot run before the governance decision.
Reuse existing decision and timeline primitives; add at most one narrow abstraction only if the current path lacks a clean seam.

steps.title: Prove all branches
details: ALLOW executes exactly once and records outcome.
BLOCK executes zero times and records denial/non-execution.
Pending review/authority executes zero times and records pending governance truthfully.

steps.title: Protect read-only views
details: Pin that replay invokes no tools and audit does not recompute policy as a side effect of this change.

acceptance: One deterministic executable test/demo proves all supported decision branches.
No execution can occur before decision evidence exists.
Block/pending branches execute zero tool calls.

must_check: The production execution path, not only a helper, is gated.
No unknown/pending state falls through to execution.
Timeline evidence distinguishes policy outcome from tool outcome.
reject_if: A new workflow/orchestration framework is introduced.
BLOCK or pending review executes a tool.
ALLOW can execute more than once through the same request path.
Replay invokes tools or audit recomputes policy.

validation_notes.targeted_contract_coverage: Canonical pre-execution runtime governance decision enforcement.
missing_targets: tests/test_runtime_decision_enforcement.py may be created by this pack
